verification.summary: Fixed a real bug in src/mock-github/dataset.ts (growth interval was 4000ms, doubling the spec's required 10s fill time to 20s) and verified it with the existing unit suite; accs.bash itself still fails in this sandbox for reasons outside my write boundary (owner/repo URL construction and process cleanup), which I could not fix or route around.

mustFix.problem: accs.bash treats GITHUB_REPO as a bare repo name and concatenates it after a separate GITHUB_OWNER, but the project's own established convention (config.ts, .env.example: 'Repo is an env var; ex. kzmijak/collinson-issue-tracker') is that GITHUB_REPO holds the combined 'owner/repo' string. In an environment where GITHUB_REPO=owner/repo (as this sandbox has ambiently), accs.bash builds /repos/owner/owner/repo/issues, so mock-github never answers and the whole run fails at 'mock boot' with a route that actually works fine.

mustFix.quote:
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  if curl -s --max-time 5 -o "$HERE/first.json" -w '%{http_code}' "$URL" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^2'; then
mustFix.problem: The boot-detection loop and the mock's growth timer both run off the same wall clock (MOCK_START), but the loop can legitimately eat up to 10s before the first successful curl on a loaded machine. If that happens, the growth window (now correctly 10s per spec) can already be exhausted by the time TOTAL1 is captured, so the later 'TOTAL2 > TOTAL1' assertion is structurally unsatisfiable even though the mock is growing exactly as specified.

kill only signals the top-level pnpm wrapper PID, not its sh -c tsx / node descendants, so a failed or interrupted run leaves live node processes holding write offsets into the recycled tracker.accs.log/mock.accs.log files. The next run's truncation of those same files then produces NUL-byte holes when the orphan next writes, breaking grep-based assertions for reasons unrelated to the tracker's actual output.
